title: FaST: Efficient and Effective Long-Horizon Forecasting for Large-Scale Spatial-Temporal Graphs via Mixture-of-Experts

problem.claim: Large-scale spatial-temporal graph forecasting requires long-horizon predictions while controlling computational cost and memory consumption.

gap.claim: Existing models predominantly focus on short-horizon predictions and incur substantial computational and memory costs when scaled to long horizons and large graphs.

contributions.claim: FaST is a heterogeneity-aware Mixture-of-Experts framework for efficient long-horizon forecasting on large-scale spatial-temporal graphs.
FaST introduces an adaptive graph agent attention mechanism to reduce the computational burden of conventional graph convolution and self-attention on large-scale graphs.
FaST introduces a parallel Mixture-of-Experts module that replaces traditional feed-forward networks with Gated Linear Units to provide an efficient, scalable parallel structure.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On real-world datasets, FaST is reported to achieve superior long-horizon predictive accuracy and remarkable computational efficiency relative to state-of-the-art baselines.
The framework is reported to support one-week-ahead prediction, defined as 672 steps at 15-minute granularity, with thousands of nodes.
The source code is reported to be publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Spatial-temporal graph forecasting on large-scale networks has received substantial attention.
Existing approaches mainly target short horizons and face computational and memory limitations on long-horizon forecasting over large graphs.
FaST addresses these challenges with a heterogeneity-aware Mixture-of-Experts framework for long-horizon, large-scale forecasting.
The framework uses adaptive graph agent attention and a parallel Mixture-of-Experts module with Gated Linear Units.
Experiments on real-world datasets report improved long-horizon accuracy and computational efficiency compared with state-of-the-art baselines.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines attention sparsification or compression with parallel expert computation to address long-horizon forecasting at large graph scale.

interpretation.claim: Scaling long-horizon graph forecasting may require reducing both graph-interaction cost and per-layer feed-forward computation.

application.claim: For other large structured forecasting systems, consider jointly optimizing interaction mechanisms and expertized computation rather than optimizing only the forecasting objective.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these design choices generalize beyond the reported spatial-temporal graph forecasting settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baseline identities, quantitative accuracy gains, or efficiency measurements.
The abstract does not describe the model architecture in sufficient detail to assess implementation requirements or computational complexity.
The abstract does not report ablations, statistical uncertainty, or independent verification of the experimental claims.
